conclusion: Control of the goods passes to Bilby Robotics Pty Ltd when its authorised representative signs the delivery note at the delivery address (CON-001-T1). Payment falls due 30 days after the signed delivery note (CON-001-T2); the contract has no return right or rebate terms.

reasoning_chain.text: Clause 5.1 (CON-001-T1): title to and risk in the goods pass to the customer when its authorised representative signs the delivery note at the delivery address; until then the seller has no right to payment.
Revenue is recognised when the customer obtains control of the promised goods (AASB 15 para 31).
For an obligation satisfied at a point in time, indicators of control include a present right to payment, legal title and the significant risks and rewards of ownership (AASB 15 para 38).
Legal title, risk and the right to payment all pass when the delivery note is signed, so control transfers and revenue is recognised at that point.

counter_argument: A side arrangement under which the customer takes control before signing, such as a bill-and-hold agreement, would move the transfer point.
